name: Laura Beddoe
title: Psychologist
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: Her approach to mental health care is collaborative, sex-positive, and gender-affirming. Laura explores the connection between mental and sexual health. Supporting individuals navigating challenges including anxiety, attachment and sexual trauma, sexual pain, intimacy, and relationship difficulties (e.g., managing conflict, trust issues, differences in libido and relationship breakdowns), and those wanting to explore their gender and sexual identity.

name: Lauren French
title: Other
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: Her approach is always warm and empathetic, with curiosity used to safely dive into the tensions held around sex and sexuality. Lauren has previously worked both clinically and in the not-for-profit space targeting sexual violence prevention through education and advocacy. Over the last eight years, she has specialised in child sexual abuse prevention, and consent and respectful relationship education. She additionally completed an international research fellowship studying Indigenous elder guided relationship and community repair after youth sexual violence.

name: Lesley Denmeade
title: Psychologist
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: Lesley is a sex positive and LBTIQA+ inclusive psychologist with experience working with clients from a wide range of diverse backgrounds, cultures, sexual orientations, and gender identities. Lesley has worked across a range of clinical psychology settings, supporting clients with varied and complex mental health presentations, including mood disorders, anxiety disorders, and trauma-related disorders. Lesley brings a strong foundation in working with trauma, including recent and historical experiences of sexual trauma, PTSD, complex trauma, and childhood sexual trauma, and she is skilled in supporting clients in navigating the ongoing impacts of these experiences. Lesley has extensive experience supporting clients across a broad range of relational and sexual health concerns, including intimacy and sexual health anxiety, relationship transitions (including separation and infidelity), and sexual pain conditions (i.e., vulvodynia, vaginismus, dyspareunia).

name: Lucy Street
title: Counsellor
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: Lucy has a deep interest in supporting the LGBTQUIA+ and disabled communities. Lucy is also in the process of completing a Master of Science in Medicine (Sexual and Reproductive Health) (Psychosexual Therapy) at the University of Sydney. Lucy has been successfully helping couples bridge gaps in communication, mis-matching libidos, desire, conflict resolution, kink negotiations, relational structure changes and much more for several years now. By melding their fascination for sexual development, sexual health and identities with communication, attachment theory and developmental theory, Lucy has learned to embrace many different relational dynamics and their wonderful complexities.

name: Paul Fellows
title: Psychologist
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: Guided by values of inclusivity, authenticity, compassion, and a sex-positive perspective, Paul is committed to honouring each client's unique story and supporting them to create meaningful and lasting change. Paul is particularly passionate about providing affirming, inclusive support for the LGBTQIA+ community, neurodivergent people, and those exploring diverse relationship structures. Paul has experience in supporting clients across a range of sexual health concerns, including sexual health anxiety, pornography addiction, desire and arousal dissatisfaction, and differences in libido, as well as mental health concerns, including anxiety, depression, stress, grief and loss, and adjusting to life changes. Paul is also interested in working with a wide range of sexual health and intimacy concerns, including sexual pain (i.e., vulvodynia, vaginismus, and dyspareunia), sexual addiction, premature ejaculation, erectile difficulties, anorgasmia, orgasmic anhedonia, and STI diagnosis support.

name: Phivo Georgiou
title: Psychologist
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: He has experience supporting clients across public mental health, private practice, and hospital settings, working with presentations including anxiety, depression, stress, trauma, personality vulnerabilities such as BPD, substance use concerns, and difficulties relating to emotion regulation and self-worth. Phivo’s practice is trauma-informed, neuroaffirming, and inclusive of people from diverse backgrounds and identities. Phivo is passionate about supporting LGBTQIA+ individuals and has an interest in supporting clients across a wide range of sexual health and intimacy concerns. He also has extensive experience supporting clients whose partners are living with mental health issues or have experienced trauma or abuse, helping them navigate the challenges of providing support while maintaining their own wellbeing.

name: Pia Cole
title: Psychologist
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: Drawing from her studies in community psychology, Pia centres her values in her work, utilising an intersectional feminist lens and queer theory to understand sociocultural context and identity as important influences on well-being. Pia has a special interest and experience working with queer identities and the lived experiences of women and AFAB (assigned female at birth) individuals. She has experience with a broad range of mental health challenges, including sexual health concerns, self-esteem, body image, depression, anxiety, and grief, as well as victim-survivors of trauma. Pia has an interest in supporting clients across a wide range of sexual health concerns, including sexual pain (such as vulvodynia, vaginismus, and dyspareunia), sexual and pornography addiction, sexual health anxiety, desire and arousal dissatisfaction (including libido differences and erectile difficulties), orgasm-related difficulties (such as anorgasmia, orgasmic anhedonia, and premature ejaculation), and STI diagnosis support.
specialties: kink, lgbtiqa+, queer, sex, sexual, trauma

name: Rachelle King
title: Psychologist
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: Her approach is sex-positive, gender-affirming, and person-centred. Rachelle has a background in providing affirming support for the LGBTQIA+ community, neurodivergent clients, and those in non-monogamous relationships. She has experience in supporting adolescent and adult clients across a wide range of mental health concerns, including with anxiety, depression, emotion regulation, complex trauma, grief, stress, and adjusting to change. Rachelle is committed to providing affirming support for LGBTQIA+ individuals, those engaged in kink and non-monogamous relationships, sex workers, and clients seeking sexual education.
specialties: gender-affirming, kink, lgbtqia+, sex, sexual, trauma
